citation: Thomure, H. T., Taha, H., Sabella, T., & Saleh, R. A systematic review of teaching and learning in the context of Arabic diglossia. Social Sciences & Humanities Open, 12, 102281.
population_language: Arabic learners; 101 studies, 1970-2021
method: PRISMA-style systematic review across eight databases; 927 records screened and 101 included
finding: Diglossic distance repeatedly affects literacy; systematic exposure to simplified Standard Arabic and explicit bridging between spoken and standard forms are recurring recommendations.
causal_interpretation: Synthesis supports a design direction but does not establish one universally effective intervention.
limitation: Large heterogeneity; much evidence is observational and regional; intervention quality varies.
license_data_availability: Open access, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; review forms available from authors on request.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Ask for home dialect and expose spoken-to-Standard-Arabic contrasts before Quranic decoding; do not assume Arabic-speaking users already know MSA phonology.

citation: Jouhar, M. R. Effects of Diglossia on the Acquisition of Underlying Reading Processes: Toward Pragmatic Solutions. International Journal for Research in Education, 47(1), 200-229.
population_language: Arabic-speaking children and students; studies of Standard and Spoken Arabic
method: Systematic review of diglossia effects on phonological, orthographic and morphological processes
finding: Systematic Standard-Arabic exposure of 15-60 minutes daily was associated across included studies with narrower oral-written gaps and better word reading and comprehension.
causal_interpretation: The review aggregates mixed designs; duration-outcome statements are not equivalent to a pooled randomized dose-response estimate.
limitation: Search and risk-of-bias detail is less extensive than in major evidence-synthesis standards; syntax gap may persist.
license_data_availability: Institutional full text is publicly downloadable; no reusable dataset or explicit content-reuse licence stated.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Build short daily MSA/Quranic-Arabic exposure and measure decoding and comprehension separately over months, not only lesson completion.

citation: Abu-Rabia, S. The Effect of Arabic Vowels on the Reading Comprehension of Second- and Sixth-Grade Native Arab Children. Journal of Psycholinguistic Research, 28, 93-101.
population_language: 145 native Arabic-speaking children: grade 2 n=71 and grade 6 n=74
method: Within-participant comparison of vowelized and unvowelized stories with comprehension questions
finding: Short vowels significantly facilitated comprehension in both age groups.
causal_interpretation: The manipulated text condition supports a causal effect for these materials and samples.
limitation: School samples from northern Israel; old study; comprehension measures and texts were narrow; not Quran-specific.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; abstract/index openly available; materials and participant data not released.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Keep full tashkeel for beginners and make removal gradual and proficiency-gated; never hide diacritics merely to raise difficulty.

citation: Asadi, I. A., Khateb, A., & Shany, M. How simple is reading in Arabic? A cross-sectional investigation of reading comprehension from first to sixth grade. Journal of Research in Reading, 40(1), 1-22.
population_language: Native Arabic-speaking children, grades 1-6
method: Cross-sectional measurement of decoding, language and comprehension across grades
finding: Arabic comprehension draws on changing combinations of decoding and language skills as children move from vowelized to unvowelized print.
causal_interpretation: Predictive associations do not prove that training a measured component will cause gains.
limitation: Cross-sectional rather than longitudinal; native-child context differs from adult and non-Arab learners.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; no open participant dataset stated.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Maintain separate learner estimates for grapheme decoding, oral vocabulary and comprehension; use staged vowelized-to-unvowelized transitions.

citation: Taha, H., & Saiegh-Haddad, E. The Role of Phonological versus Morphological Skills in the Development of Arabic Spelling: An Intervention Study. Journal of Psycholinguistic Research, 45, 507-535.
population_language: Native Arabic readers in grades 2, 4 and 6; skilled and poor readers
method: Pre/post comparison of phonological training, morphological training and non-intervention control
finding: Both linguistic interventions improved spelling; transfer appeared between phonological and morphological skills.
causal_interpretation: The controlled intervention supports causality for spelling outcomes under the study conditions, not Quran recitation or comprehension.
limitation: Assignment and sample details constrain certainty; spelling is not oral recitation; no long-term follow-up reported in the abstract.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; no open intervention package or participant data stated.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Teach roots/patterns and sound segmentation as explicit but linked strands; test transfer on unseen Quranic words rather than familiar lesson items.

citation: Saiegh-Haddad, E., & Taha, H. The Role of Morphological and Phonological Awareness in the Early Development of Word Spelling and Reading in Typically Developing and Disabled Arabic Readers. Dyslexia, 23(4), 345-371.
population_language: 160 Arabic-speaking children in grades 1-4; typical and reading-accuracy-disabled groups
method: Cross-sectional case-control tasks covering morphology, phonology, vowelized/unvowelized reading and spelling
finding: Phonological awareness was the strongest reading predictor; morphological awareness explained additional variance, especially for spelling.
causal_interpretation: Results identify diagnostic correlates, not effects of a particular lesson intervention.
limitation: Cross-sectional; local diagnostic definitions; does not establish optimal instructional dosage.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; no open data or task licence stated.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Placement should test phoneme manipulation and root/pattern awareness separately; adapt support without diagnosing dyslexia in-app.

citation: Rakhlin, N. V., Li, N., Aljughaiman, A., & Grigorenko, E. L. Speech Is Golden: The Importance of Colloquial Arabic for Reading Standard Arabic for Beginning Readers. Journal of Speech, Language, and Hearing Research, 68(3S), 1441-1467.
population_language: 110 Saudi Arabic-speaking children, grades 2-4
method: Oral-language, decoding and phonological-awareness measures analyzed with single and serial mediation/path models
finding: Colloquial oral-language skills contributed to Standard-Arabic reading comprehension through measured pathways.
causal_interpretation: Path analysis is correlational even when mediation language is used; it does not prove instructional causality.
limitation: One regional sample; vowelized reading; model specification may not generalize to non-native learners.
license_data_availability: Publisher page/abstract available; no open dataset or reuse licence stated.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Use the learner's stronger spoken language to explain meaning and bridge to MSA; do not penalize dialect knowledge as an error.

citation: Saiegh-Haddad, E., & Haj, L. Does phonological distance impact quality of phonological representations? Evidence from Arabic diglossia. Journal of Child Language, 45(6), 1377-1399.
population_language: 120 Arabic-speaking children: kindergarten, grades 1, 2 and 6
method: Cross-age phonological representation tasks contrasting spoken-standard distance
finding: Standard-Arabic phonological representations were weaker when forms were distant from the spoken variety, especially early in development.
causal_interpretation: Age and distance associations support a diagnostic hypothesis, not a causal treatment effect.
limitation: Cross-sectional cohorts; dialect-specific distance; task performance may not map directly to Quranic tajwid.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; no open data stated.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Tag lesson words by dialect-to-MSA distance and add listen-discriminate-produce scaffolds for distant phonemes/lexemes.

citation: Eghbaria-Ghanamah, H., Ghanamah, R., Shalhoub-Awwad, Y., Adi-Japha, E., & Karni, A. Long-term benefits after a rhyme-repetition based intervention program for kindergarteners: Better reading and spelling in the first grade. Developmental Psychology, 58(2), 252-269.
population_language: Arabic-speaking kindergarten children followed into grade 1
method: Randomized intervention comparing MSA rhyme recitation, repeated listening and related conditions, with delayed literacy outcomes
finding: Active recitation-based familiarization with MSA rhymes produced longer-term literacy benefits beyond passive exposure in reported outcomes.
causal_interpretation: Random allocation and active-control comparisons support a causal interpretation for this program and population.
limitation: Rhyme program is not Quran recitation; setting and age are narrow; exact components cannot be isolated completely.
license_data_availability: APA copyright; study materials/data not openly licensed in the publisher record.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: For children, require listen-then-recite interaction rather than autoplay-only exposure; measure transfer to novel letters/words months later.

citation: Wagner, D. A., & Spratt, J. E. Arabic Orthography and Reading Acquisition. In The Cross-Language Study of Reading and Spelling, 229-244.
population_language: Beginning Arabic readers in Morocco
method: Field study within a longitudinal literacy-acquisition program
finding: Early Arabic reading depended strongly on alphabetic decoding skills, with similarities to other alphabetic scripts.
causal_interpretation: Observational and developmental evidence does not determine the best digital intervention.
limitation: Older Moroccan context; measures and schooling differ from current app learners; chapter is not open access.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; no open data stated.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Do not skip grapheme-phoneme mastery: gate connected-script and ayah tasks on accurate letter-form and vowel decoding.

citation: Bin Sawad, N., Law, J. M., Tibi, S., & Boese, K. Arabic metalinguistic knowledge predicts reading comprehension: A scoping review. Frontiers in Communication, 7, 984340.
population_language: Arabic-speaking school-age learners across included studies
method: Scoping review of phonological awareness, morphological awareness, orthographic knowledge and reading comprehension
finding: Phonological and morphological awareness repeatedly related to Arabic comprehension; the evidence base is uneven and intervention research is limited.
causal_interpretation: The review maps associations and gaps; it does not establish that every proposed metalinguistic activity causes comprehension gains.
limitation: Heterogeneous measures, ages and designs; limited causal studies.
license_data_availability: Open access, CC BY 4.0; no pooled participant dataset.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Represent phonology, morphology and orthography as separate mastery dimensions and validate each with unseen-word and passage tasks.

citation: Wilson, E., Jeon, S., Cook, H., & Abadzi, H. Perceptual Enhancement for Arabic Reading: An Intervention to Support Fluency and Automaticity in Grade One. Gulf Education and Social Policy Review, 1(1), 1-21.
population_language: 345 grade-1 Arabic readers; intervention n=174 and comparison n=171
method: School-based intervention using perceptual enhancement of Arabic print
finding: Enhanced visual cues were associated with gains in early fluency/automaticity measures.
causal_interpretation: Quasi-experimental allocation limits causal certainty; effects should be replicated before product-wide adoption.
limitation: Implementation and assignment may be confounded; short-term school outcome; not Quran-specific.
license_data_availability: Open access under a Creative Commons Attribution licence; no open learner data found.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Pilot optional temporary highlighting for letter shape/dot and joining contrasts, then fade cues and test transfer to ordinary Uthmani text.

citation: Aboras, Y. A., Elbanna, M. M., Abdou, R. M., & Salama, H. M. Development of a remediation program for Egyptian dyslexic children. Alexandria Journal of Medicine, 48(1), 51-59.
population_language: Egyptian Arabic-speaking children with dyslexia
method: Clinical pre/post phonological-awareness remediation program with age and outcome analyses
finding: Phonological-awareness remediation improved measured reading-related outcomes; younger intervention was associated with better response.
causal_interpretation: Program evidence is supportive, but design details and pre/post structure limit strong causal/general claims.
limitation: Clinical sample; culturally specific materials; no evidence for automated diagnosis or Quranic fluency.
license_data_availability: Open access under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; materials/data not released for adaptation.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Offer slower phoneme segmentation, repeatable audio and non-timed paths; provide a referral/support statement rather than medical labels.

citation: Booton, S. A., Hodgkiss, A., & Murphy, V. A. The impact of mobile application features on children's language and literacy learning: a systematic review. Computer Assisted Language Learning, 36(3), 400-429.
population_language: Children aged 3-11; 11 experimental or quasi-experimental studies
method: Systematic review of narration, conversational prompts, augmented reality and hotspots in touchscreen apps
finding: Inbuilt narration helped versus child reading alone but not versus adult shared reading; prompts improved adult-child talk; decorative/interactivity effects were context-dependent.
causal_interpretation: Included experiments support feature-level effects in their tasks, not a blanket benefit of more animation or screen time.
limitation: Only 11 eligible studies; languages/tasks varied; not Arabic/Quran-specific.
license_data_availability: Open access, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; review extraction data not clearly released.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Use narration and parent prompts as scaffolds; keep animation instruction-relevant, disable decorative motion during decoding, and never claim the app replaces shared reading/teacher correction.

citation: Cepeda, N. J., Pashler, H., Vul, E., Wixted, J. T., & Rohrer, D. Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: A review and quantitative synthesis. Psychological Bulletin, 132(3), 354-380.
population_language: Human learners across 317 experiments in 184 articles; mainly verbal materials
method: Meta-analysis of distributed versus massed practice and timing moderators
finding: Distributed practice outperformed massed practice in most comparisons; optimal spacing depends on desired retention interval.
causal_interpretation: Broad convergence supports a causal spacing effect, but not a single universal interval algorithm.
limitation: Predominantly laboratory/verbal tasks; publication and design heterogeneity; no Quran-specific studies.
license_data_availability: APA copyright; article may be author-archived; synthesis data not packaged as a product-ready scheduler.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Schedule ayah/word/rule reviews by target retention horizon and performance; validate intervals prospectively instead of copying fixed SM-2 defaults.

citation: Cepeda, N. J., Vul, E., Rohrer, D., Wixted, J. T., & Pashler, H. Spacing Effects in Learning: A Temporal Ridgeline of Optimal Retention. Psychological Science, 19(11), 1095-1102.
population_language: More than 1,350 online adult participants; fact learning in English
method: Experimental manipulation of study gap up to 3.5 months and test delay up to one year
finding: Best interstudy gap increased with final retention delay; overlong gaps eventually reduced performance.
causal_interpretation: Randomized timing manipulation supports causality for fact learning.
limitation: Facts and adults are not sequential oral Quran passages; one-review design differs from continuing hifz.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; author manuscript publicly available; no production licence for content.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Let users choose retention goal and adapt intervals; prevent review backlogs from silently expanding past demonstrated recall.

citation: Roediger, H. L., & Karpicke, J. D. Test-Enhanced Learning: Taking Memory Tests Improves Long-Term Retention. Psychological Science, 17(3), 249-255.
population_language: University students learning prose passages in English
method: Two experiments comparing repeated study with one or repeated free-recall tests at 5-minute, 2-day and 1-week delays
finding: Restudy helped immediate performance, while retrieval produced better retention after 2 days and 1 week despite lower confidence.
causal_interpretation: Randomized condition and delayed tests support a causal retrieval-practice benefit for prose.
limitation: University/lab setting; no feedback in key conditions; Quran recitation has sequencing and phonetic constraints.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; author copies available; no open participant data stated.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Include closed-text recitation and meaning recall after study; do not infer mastery from immediate recognition or learner confidence.

citation: Karpicke, J. D., & Roediger, H. L. The Critical Importance of Retrieval for Learning. Science, 319(5865), 966-968.
population_language: University students learning foreign-language vocabulary
method: Experimental study-test schedules that dropped learned items from study and/or testing
finding: Repeated testing after initial success greatly improved one-week retention; repeated studying after success did not.
causal_interpretation: Experimental manipulation supports a causal role for continued retrieval in this vocabulary paradigm.
limitation: Paired vocabulary is simpler than connected ayat and oral accuracy; one-week horizon.
license_data_availability: AAAS copyright; no open dataset or reuse licence stated.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: A first correct recitation must not remove an ayah from review; require spaced successful retrievals at increasing delays.

citation: Rowland, C. A. The effect of testing versus restudy on retention: a meta-analytic review of the testing effect. Psychological Bulletin, 140(6), 1432-1463.
population_language: 159 effect sizes from laboratory learning studies
method: Random-effects meta-analysis of testing versus restudy moderators
finding: Testing improved delayed retention overall; effortful recall tended to outperform recognition, and feedback moderated outcomes.
causal_interpretation: Synthesis supports retrieval over restudy on average, with substantial moderator dependence.
limitation: Laboratory-heavy corpus and heterogeneous materials; not Quran/hifz-specific.
license_data_availability: APA copyright; no openly licensed source materials; extraction availability not clear.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Prefer free recitation, continuation and meaning production over multiple choice; give corrective feedback and log cue level.

citation: Agarwal, P. K., Nunes, L. D., & Blunt, J. R. Retrieval Practice Consistently Benefits Student Learning: a Systematic Review of Applied Research in Schools and Classrooms. Educational Psychology Review, 33, 1409-1453.
population_language: 5,374 learners across 50 classroom experiments, school through higher education
method: Systematic review with 49 coded effect sizes under a narrow classroom definition
finding: Most effects favored retrieval practice; 57% were medium or large, across ages and classroom settings.
causal_interpretation: Experimental classroom evidence supports causality within included comparisons, but effect size varies.
limitation: Few Quran/Arabic tasks; implementation and controls differ; publication corpus may underrepresent null results.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright with accessible author versions; coding resources should be checked before reuse.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Use low-stakes daily retrieval and delayed checks in real lessons; run an A/B or cluster trial on Quran retention rather than relying only on lab transfer.

citation: Moreira, B. F. T., Pinto, T. S. S., Starling, D. S. V., & Jaeger, A. Retrieval Practice in Classroom Settings: A Review of Applied Research. Frontiers in Education, 4, 5.
population_language: Elementary through medical-school classroom studies
method: Review restricted to educationally relevant classroom experiments
finding: Classroom retrieval usually helped against restudy or no activity, but comparisons with strong alternative learning activities were less conclusive.
causal_interpretation: Evidence does not justify calling retrieval uniquely superior to every active alternative.
limitation: Review predates later trials; study descriptions and controls varied; not language-specific.
license_data_availability: Open access, CC BY 4.0.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Compare retrieval against a credible active control such as guided recitation with feedback; report null results and not only engagement.

citation: Al Arifi, N., Zurqoni, & Robingatin. Challenges in Qur'anic Memorization Learning at Elementary Schools: Systematic Literature Review. Tafkir, 7(1).
population_language: Elementary Quran-memorization settings; 14 Scopus-indexed studies from 2015-2025
method: PRISMA-guided systematic literature review
finding: Recurring barriers include time, motivation, teacher support, method consistency and weak home/school coordination.
causal_interpretation: The synthesis diagnoses implementation problems; it does not establish which digital method causes better retention.
limitation: Only 14 studies, substantial regional and methodological heterogeneity, limited experimental work.
license_data_availability: Open access, CC BY-SA 4.0; no pooled learner data.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Add teacher/parent handoff, manageable review load and adherence diagnostics; do not present streaks alone as a memorization intervention.

citation: Al-Razi, M. F., & Kusumasari, F. Beyond rote learning: a scoping review of the education-related effects of Quran memorisation. British Journal of Religious Education.
population_language: 36 empirical hifz studies; evidence dominated by Indo-Malay settings
method: PRISMA-ScR scoping review of cognitive, academic and psychospiritual outcomes
finding: The literature reports multiple positive associations, but observational designs dominate and domain-specific retention is often not separated from broader claims.
causal_interpretation: The review explicitly does not justify causal claims that hifz raises general intelligence or academic achievement.
limitation: Regional concentration; broad outcomes; varied quality; limited randomized or long-term retention trials.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; no open extraction dataset or commercial reuse licence stated.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Measure ayah retention directly at 1, 7, 30 and 90 days; avoid marketing claims about general cognition, grades or wellbeing without trials.

citation: Ikhsan, I., Hayati, Z., & Iswantir, M. Pengaruh Penggunaan Aplikasi Hafalan Al-Qur'an pada Android terhadap Kemampuan Menghafal Al-Qur'an Siswa. FENOMENA, 16(2).
population_language: Indonesian school students using an Android Quran memorization app
method: Pre/post analysis using paired tests and N-gain
finding: Scores increased after app use; reported N-gain was 0.3656 (medium category).
causal_interpretation: Without a randomized concurrent control, improvement cannot be attributed solely to the app.
limitation: Practice, maturation and testing effects are uncontrolled; local rubric; no long-term delayed outcome.
license_data_availability: Open access, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; app/content reuse rights not established.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Treat app efficacy as unproven until a controlled delayed-retention pilot is run; instrument dose, prior hifz and teacher contact.

citation: Fuchs, L. S., & Fuchs, D. Effects of Systematic Formative Evaluation: A Meta-Analysis. Exceptional Children, 53(3), 199-208.
population_language: 21 controlled special-education studies; 96 effect sizes
method: Meta-analysis of systematic formative evaluation procedures
finding: Average weighted effect was reported as 0.70, with effects varying by data display, evaluation rules and behavior-management components.
causal_interpretation: Controlled evidence supports formative evaluation in the included contexts; the historical pooled estimate should not be treated as universal.
limitation: Old, special-education-heavy evidence; methods and publication practices predate current standards.
license_data_availability: SAGE copyright; no open extraction dataset.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Show teachers/learners a trend of specific errors and use explicit rules to alter the next lesson, rather than collecting scores without adaptation.

citation: Kingston, N., & Nash, B. Formative Assessment: A Meta-Analysis and a Call for Research. Educational Measurement: Issues and Practice, 30(4), 28-37.
population_language: K-12; over 300 studies screened, 13 usable studies and 42 independent effects
method: Random-effects meta-analysis with design-quality screening
finding: Weighted mean effect was 0.20, far below commonly repeated 0.70 claims; computer-based and professional-development implementations were somewhat larger.
causal_interpretation: Supports modest average benefits while directly cautioning against inflated causal claims.
limitation: Only 13 studies met calculation criteria; wide implementation variation and possible selection bias.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; no open dataset stated.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Set conservative impact expectations and pre-register Muslingo trials; never cite a generic 0.70 formative-assessment effect in marketing.

citation: Wisniewski, B., Zierer, K., & Hattie, J. The Power of Feedback Revisited: A Meta-Analysis of Educational Feedback Research. Frontiers in Psychology, 10, 3087.
population_language: More than 61,000 learners; 435 studies, 994 effects
method: Random-effects meta-analysis with moderator analyses
finding: Average feedback effect was medium (d=0.48) but highly heterogeneous; information content mattered, and cognitive/motor outcomes benefited more than motivation/behavior.
causal_interpretation: Feedback is not one treatment; causality and magnitude depend on intervention design.
limitation: Mixed study quality, outcomes and settings; aggregate effect does not specify Quran feedback wording.
license_data_availability: Open access, CC BY 4.0; article/figures openly available.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Return task-level information: what was omitted/substituted, an example and next attempt; avoid praise-only or unexplained percentage scores.

citation: Morris, R., Perry, T., & Wardle, L. Formative assessment and feedback for learning in higher education: A systematic review. Review of Education, 9(3), e3292.
population_language: Higher-education learners; 28 studies judged to provide satisfactory causal evidence
method: Systematic review of performance outcomes and feedback approaches
finding: Evidence supports formative assessment overall, but does not identify a single consistently superior type or mode.
causal_interpretation: Causal evidence exists in included studies, but generalization to children and Quran learning is indirect.
limitation: Higher-education focus; many strategies are advocated more often than rigorously tested.
license_data_availability: Open access, CC BY 4.0; published PDF available.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Pilot feedback variants by learner level; do not hard-code one explanation style for children, adult beginners and advanced hifz learners.

citation: Karaman, P. The Effect of Formative Assessment Practices on Student Learning: A Meta-Analysis Study. International Journal of Assessment Tools in Education, 8(4), 801-817.
population_language: Turkish educational studies; 32 studies and 47 effects
method: Meta-analysis of experimental and quasi-experimental formative-assessment interventions
finding: Overall mean effect was 0.72; student-initiated and mixed feedback were larger than computer-only feedback (reported d=0.42).
causal_interpretation: Effects support the included interventions, but national corpus and subgroup confounding prevent a universal ranking.
limitation: Single-country publication corpus; mixed designs; moderator groups may differ on more than feedback source.
license_data_availability: Open journal access; article licence should be checked before reuse; no learner dataset stated.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Allow self-rating and replay/dispute alongside automated feedback; reserve teacher review for uncertainty and high-stakes checkpoints.

citation: Shute, V. J. Focus on Formative Feedback. Review of Educational Research, 78(1), 153-189.
population_language: Education and training studies across ages and domains
method: Structured review of formative-feedback findings and moderators
finding: Feedback is most useful when specific, supportive, task-focused and manageable; verification alone is often insufficient for complex learning.
causal_interpretation: The review synthesizes mechanisms and design guidance, not a pooled Quran-specific causal estimate.
limitation: Older and heterogeneous literature; recommendations interact with task and learner characteristics.
license_data_availability: SAGE/AERA copyright; no open dataset.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: After a wrong response, provide one actionable correction and a focused retry; chunk multi-error recitations instead of presenting an overwhelming error list.

citation: Panadero, E., Jönsson, A., & Botella, J. Effects of self-assessment on self-regulated learning and self-efficacy: Four meta-analyses. Educational Research Review, 22, 74-98.
population_language: Learners across school and higher-education studies
method: Four meta-analyses of self-assessment effects on self-regulated learning and self-efficacy
finding: Self-assessment was positively related to/self-reported as improving self-regulation and self-efficacy, with reported self-efficacy effect around 0.73.
causal_interpretation: Designs vary; self-report and intervention effects must not be conflated with objective skill mastery.
limitation: Heterogeneous instruments and interventions; publication bias and weak controls in parts of the corpus.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; author manuscript publicly available; no open item bank.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Ask learners to rate confidence before revealing correctness, but keep confidence separate from mastery and speech-model confidence.

citation: Saito, K. Effects of Instruction on L2 Pronunciation Development: A Synthesis of 15 Quasi-Experimental Intervention Studies. TESOL Quarterly, 46(4), 842-854.
population_language: Second-language learners across 15 quasi-experimental studies; mostly non-Arabic target languages
method: Quantitative/narrative synthesis of pronunciation instruction
finding: Instruction improved controlled pronunciation outcomes more consistently than spontaneous-speech outcomes; explicit phonetic focus mattered.
causal_interpretation: Quasi-experimental synthesis supports instruction but not direct transfer to Quranic tajwid.
limitation: Small literature, diverse measures, target languages and short interventions; many researcher-made tests.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; no open pooled dataset.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Teach and practice target sounds in isolation, words and connected ayat; separately measure controlled imitation and uncued recitation.

citation: Lee, J., Jang, J., & Plonsky, L. The Effectiveness of Second Language Pronunciation Instruction: A Meta-Analysis. Applied Linguistics, 36(3), 345-366.
population_language: L2 learners across 86 study reports/effects; multiple target languages
method: Meta-analysis of pronunciation instruction and moderators
finding: Pronunciation instruction had a large positive average effect, with outcomes affected by instructional and measurement choices.
causal_interpretation: Supports causal benefits where included comparisons are controlled, but the average is not a tajwid effect.
limitation: Heterogeneity, small samples and controlled-task measures; Arabic/Quran representation is limited.
license_data_availability: Oxford University Press copyright; no open pooled speech data.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Combine perception and production training and evaluate on unseen ayat with blinded human raters, not only app-internal scores.

citation: Mahdi, H. S., & Al Khateeb, A. A. The effectiveness of computer-assisted pronunciation training: A meta-analysis. Review of Education, 7(3), 733-753.
population_language: 1,014 participants across 20 CAPT studies; young and adult L2 learners
method: Meta-analysis of computer-assisted pronunciation interventions
finding: CAPT showed a positive mean effect (reported d=0.68); effects appeared stronger for beginner/intermediate learners, but study quality was very low.
causal_interpretation: Evidence is indicative, not conclusive, because most studies were small and locally assessed.
limitation: Few studies, mostly under 100 participants, single institutions and intervention-aligned tests.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; no shared evaluation corpus.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Use CAPT as guided practice, label uncertainty, and require independent teacher-rated validation before claiming pronunciation efficacy.

citation: Almusharraf, A., Mahdi, H. S., Al-Nofaie, H., & Aljasser, A. The effect of settings, educational level and tools on computer-assisted pronunciation training: A meta-analysis. Journal of Computer Assisted Learning, 40(4), 1601-1620.
population_language: 31 experimental-versus-control studies; 42 effects across schools, institutes and universities
method: Meta-analysis with setting, educational-level and tool moderators
finding: CAPT had a medium overall effect; larger effects were reported in formal settings and for video-supported interventions.
causal_interpretation: Supports CAPT in aggregate, but subgroup findings may be confounded and do not validate Quranic ASR scoring.
limitation: Multiple languages/tools; variable study quality and outcome measures; publication bias possible.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; no open combined dataset stated.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Pair model audio/video articulation demonstrations with structured practice; validate in self-study and teacher-supported settings separately.

citation: Wang, Y.-H., & Young, S. S.-C. Effectiveness of feedback for enhancing English pronunciation in an ASR-based CALL system. Journal of Computer Assisted Learning, 31(6), 493-504.
population_language: Young and adult EFL learners; English target pronunciation
method: Study of ASR-CALL with formative/summative and implicit/explicit feedback conditions
finding: Richer formative and explicit feedback improved targeted English-pronunciation learning more than score-only interaction in the reported setting.
causal_interpretation: Controlled condition effects are causal for the implementation, not evidence that any ASR transcript accurately diagnoses tajwid.
limitation: English target; local system and measures; likely limited speaker/device diversity.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; software, speech corpus and scoring model not openly released.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Display the recognized segment, correction type and replay/retry; never conceal the transcript behind boxes or stop retries after success.

citation: Neri, A., Mich, O., Gerosa, M., & Giuliani, D. The effectiveness of computer assisted pronunciation training for foreign language learning by children. Computer Assisted Language Learning, 21(5), 393-408.
population_language: Children learning a foreign language; non-Arabic target context
method: Controlled evaluation of ASR-based CAPT for child learners
finding: Children could benefit from structured CAPT, but recognition and feedback design for child speech were central constraints.
causal_interpretation: Study supports the tested child-CAPT package, not unrestricted use of adult-trained ASR with children.
limitation: Older ASR; small/local sample; target language differs; child speech variability remains substantial.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; system/data not openly licensed.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Create a child-specific speech gate: separate calibration, higher abstention, no punitive life loss, and easy human/parent retry.

citation: Lee, B., Plonsky, L., & Saito, K. The effects of perception- vs. production-based pronunciation instruction. System, 88, 102185.
population_language: L2 learners across pronunciation-intervention studies; multiple languages
method: Meta-analysis contrasting perception-focused and production-focused instruction
finding: Both perception and production practice contributed, with outcomes depending on matching between training and test modality.
causal_interpretation: Supports including both modalities; it does not show that listening alone ensures accurate production.
limitation: Language and outcome heterogeneity; limited Quranic/Arabic evidence.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; no open pooled audio corpus.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Every speech task should require a reference listen first, but mastery must include independent production and a later transfer item.

citation: Sun, W. The impact of automatic speech recognition technology on second language pronunciation and speaking skills of EFL learners: a mixed methods investigation. Frontiers in Psychology, 14, 1210187.
population_language: 61 EFL learners: experimental class n=29 and control class n=32
method: Quasi-experimental class comparison plus qualitative data
finding: ASR with peer correction improved measured English pronunciation/speaking outcomes in the experimental class.
causal_interpretation: Non-random class assignment means teacher, class and peer effects may contribute; ASR alone is not isolated.
limitation: English, small two-class sample, short intervention and local assessments.
license_data_availability: Open access, CC BY 4.0; underlying learner audio/data availability not prominent.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Blend automated flags with peer/teacher review in pilots; avoid attributing a combined workflow's gains solely to the model.

citation: Lataifeh, M., & Elnagar, A. Ar-DAD: Arabic diversified audio dataset. Data in Brief, 33, 106503.
population_language: 15,810 clips from 30 prominent Quran reciters covering 37 surahs; 379 imitation clips from 12 imitators
method: Public dataset construction from EveryAyah with reciter/imitator organization and text files
finding: Provides a reproducible professional-recitation corpus for ASR/speaker research and a limited imitation subset.
causal_interpretation: Dataset availability is not evidence that a model trained on it can assess learner pronunciation.
limitation: Mostly expert male reciters; narrow surah coverage; lacks real novice error labels, children, balanced women and device metadata.
license_data_availability: Dataset released on Mendeley Data under CC BY 4.0: https://doi.org/10.17632/3kndp5vs6b.3; source-audio provenance still requires due diligence.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Use only for canonical/acoustic pretraining; never use it alone to set learner-error thresholds or claim demographic fairness.

citation: Salameh, R., Al Mdfaa, M., Askarbekuly, N., & Mazzara, M. Quranic Audio Dataset: Crowdsourced and Labeled Recitation from Non-Arabic Speakers.
population_language: About 7,000 recitations from 1,287 participants in 11+ non-Arabic countries; 1,166 recordings annotated
method: Volunteer crowdsourcing through NamazApp and Quran Voice; six-category annotation with crowd/expert agreement checks
finding: Demonstrates collection of diverse non-native recitation and reports crowd accuracy 0.77, inter-rater agreement 0.63, and algorithm-expert agreement 0.89.
causal_interpretation: Agreement on the sampled labels does not prove pedagogical benefit or phoneme/tajwid-level diagnostic validity.
limitation: Only a subset is annotated; demographic/device/child coverage and class balance need auditing; preprint not a randomized learning study.
license_data_availability: Dataset page: https://huggingface.co/datasets/RetaSy/quranic_audio_dataset; no explicit machine-readable licence found as of 2026-09-11, so commercial use requires written permission.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Candidate for an evaluation partnership after consent/licence audit; use stratified expert relabeling and never infer missing demographic balance.

citation: El Kheir, Y., et al. Towards a Unified Benchmark for Arabic Pronunciation Assessment: Quranic Recitation as Case Study.
population_language: QuranMB.v1: 98 Quran verses, 18 native Arabic speakers (14 women, 4 men), about 2.2 hours; additional MSA resources
method: Specialized MSA phoneme inventory, processing pipeline, public test set and baseline phoneme-level models
finding: Creates a standardized phoneme-level mispronunciation benchmark and exposes substantial remaining model errors.
causal_interpretation: Benchmark scores measure agreement with its labels; they do not establish learning gains or complete tajwid coverage.
limitation: Small test set; native speakers; limited verses and recitation rules; no children/non-native beginners; possible domain leakage must be controlled.
license_data_availability: Official repo: https://github.com/Iqra-Eval/interspeech_IqraEval; train data public, test access governed by challenge; no explicit commercial licence in repo/HF card as of 2026-09-11.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Adopt its phoneme-error definitions and leakage controls for R&D, but secure licensing and add non-native/child/device strata before production.

citation: El Kheir, Y., et al. Iqra'Eval: A Shared Task on Qur'anic Pronunciation Assessment. Proceedings of ArabicNLP 2025 Shared Tasks.
population_language: 82.37 hours MSA Common Voice subset; synthetic correct/error TTS; QuranMB human test of 18 speakers
method: Shared-task dataset, fixed train/dev/test protocol and phoneme-error evaluation
finding: Provides comparable systems and shows that authentic human mispronunciation remains harder than synthetic or canonical speech.
causal_interpretation: Leaderboard improvement is model evidence, not educational efficacy.
limitation: Training errors are partly synthetic; small human Quran test; demographic and tajwid-rule coverage remain narrow.
license_data_availability: ACL Anthology paper openly available; underlying Common Voice has its own terms; Iqra datasets lack a clear commercial licence.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Keep synthetic errors for augmentation only; production acceptance must be driven by held-out authentic learner errors and per-group false-positive rates.

citation: Meghanani, A., et al. Hafs2Vec: A System for the Iqra'Eval Arabic and Qur'anic Phoneme-level Pronunciation Assessment. Proceedings of ArabicNLP 2025 Shared Tasks.
population_language: Iqra'Eval data plus about 94 hours from 28 professional reciters; QuranMB human test
method: CTC/representation-learning system with augmented professional recitation; evaluated for phoneme-level error detection
finding: Reported QuranMB F1 was 46.50% with recall 79.20%, illustrating high miss/false-alarm trade-offs despite strong recall.
causal_interpretation: System metrics do not establish safe learner feedback; an F1 below 0.5 is incompatible with unqualified corrective claims.
limitation: Professional audio dominates augmentation; small human test; speaker and rule subgroup results are limited.
license_data_availability: ACL paper open; code/data components inherit Iqra/EveryAyah/QUL terms and require separate licence review.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Use as a baseline and evidence for an abstain/human-review path; do not expose rule-level correction unless precision meets a predeclared safety target.

citation: Al Harere, A., & Al Jallad, K. Quran Recitation Recognition using End-to-End Deep Learning.
population_language: Ar-DAD professional reciters: 30 reciters, 37 surahs
method: CNN-bidirectional-GRU encoder with CTC and character beam-search decoder; WER/CER evaluation
finding: Reported 8.34% WER and 2.42% CER on the study split.
causal_interpretation: Low transcript error on professional reciters does not imply detection of subtle makhraj, madd, ghunnah or novice errors.
limitation: Potential speaker/ayah leakage must be independently checked; expert-reciter corpus; no learner-error or fairness evaluation.
license_data_availability: Preprint; code/model licence not stated in the paper record; underlying Ar-DAD is CC BY 4.0.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Separate recitation-following/transcript completeness from pronunciation/tajwid scoring; split by reciter and ayah when benchmarking.

citation: Tabbaa, H. M. A., & Soudan, B. Computer-Aided Training for Quranic Recitation. Procedia - Social and Behavioral Sciences, 192, 778-787.
population_language: Quran recitation samples used in an ASR-plus-classifier prototype; population details limited in public abstract
method: ASR integrated with a classifier to detect continuous-recitation errors
finding: Shows technical feasibility of combining recognition and error classification for a training prototype.
causal_interpretation: Prototype accuracy does not establish learner improvement or generalization across reciters/devices.
limitation: Small/opaque corpus, old ASR, limited external validation and no robust demographic breakdown.
license_data_availability: Open access under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; training data/software not openly released.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Treat as historical architecture evidence only; require modern preregistered external evaluation before any pedagogical claim.

citation: Salman, M. U., Qazi, M. A., & Alam, M. T. Quran-MD: A Fine-Grained Multilingual Multimodal Dataset of the Quran.
population_language: 6,236 ayat and word-level records; about 264,509 MP3 files from 30 reciters; Arabic, English and transliteration
method: Compilation of verse audio, word alignment/segments, text, translation and transliteration
finding: Offers unusually fine-grained word/ayah media useful for playback, alignment and pretraining.
causal_interpretation: Resource scale does not validate automatic tajwid feedback.
limitation: Professional-reciter-only design; README/paper differ on 30 versus 32 reciters; source alignment and speaker independence require audit.
license_data_availability: Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Buraaq/quran-audio-text-dataset; no explicit licence in the HF card as of 2026-09-11, so do not use commercially without clarification.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Useful after provenance/licence reconciliation for word audio and forced alignment; block production ingestion until counts and rights are resolved.

citation: Alherran, F. Tadabur: A Large-Scale Quran Audio Dataset.
population_language: More than 1,400 hours from 600+ reciters; full Quran; word-level automatic alignment
method: Large-scale aggregation and alignment pipeline with metadata and baseline model
finding: Greatly increases reciter/acoustic diversity for Quran ASR pretraining and benchmark construction.
causal_interpretation: A larger canonical corpus does not itself improve or validate learner-error diagnosis.
limitation: Reciter demographics and learner proficiency are not established; alignments are automatic; source-rights provenance needs item-level review.
license_data_availability: Official repo https://github.com/fherran/tadabur declares CC BY-NC 4.0; non-commercial, so incompatible with direct commercial training without permission.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Use for research-only robustness experiments; seek a commercial licence or build a consented Muslingo corpus before production.

citation: Abdelfattah, A., Khalil, M. I., & Abbas, H. Automatic Pronunciation Error Detection and Correction of the Holy Quran's Learners Using Deep Learning.
population_language: 848 hours/286K utterances mainly expert recitation; qdat_bench has 159 real-error samples
method: Automated data pipeline, Quran Phonetic Script, multi-level CTC, and benchmark across phonemes/diacritics/tajwid rules
finding: Reports 1.94% phoneme error on qdat_bench and 75.8% Tajweed F1; releases code and models.
causal_interpretation: Model/benchmark performance is promising engineering evidence, not proof that corrections improve learners or are safe across groups.
limitation: Real-error benchmark is only 159 samples; expert-heavy training; unclear age/gender/L1/device balance; independent replication pending.
license_data_availability: Official repo https://github.com/obadx/quran-muaalem is MIT; underlying datasets/audio retain their own licences and provenance obligations.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Reproduce on a leakage-free Muslingo holdout, audit rule-level precision and expert agreement, then enable only validated rules behind confidence thresholds.

citation: El Kheir, Y., et al. IQRA 2026: Interspeech Challenge on Automatic Pronunciation Assessment for Modern Standard Arabic (MSA).
population_language: MSA/Quran challenge resources plus Iqra_Extra_IS26 authentic human mispronunciations
method: Second challenge edition comparing CTC, self-supervised and audio-language-model systems on fixed MDD tasks
finding: Authentic human-error data accompanied a reported 0.28 F1 improvement over the first edition, showing both data and modeling progress.
causal_interpretation: Cross-edition gain cannot be attributed solely to one factor and does not prove classroom efficacy.
limitation: Challenge data access/licensing and full subgroup composition require confirmation; benchmark may not cover tajwid comprehensively.
license_data_availability: Paper preprint open; challenge repository/data terms govern use and do not currently provide a clear commercial licence.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Track the benchmark, but freeze Muslingo's own independent multilingual learner test set so public-challenge tuning cannot become the product test.

citation: W3C. Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2. W3C Recommendation, 12 December 2024.
population_language: Web and mobile content for people with visual, auditory, motor, speech, cognitive and learning disabilities
method: Consensus technical standard with testable A/AA/AAA success criteria
finding: Defines requirements for text alternatives, captions/transcripts, contrast, reflow, target size, keyboard access, focus, predictable navigation and error assistance.
causal_interpretation: WCAG conformance demonstrates technical accessibility criteria, not learning efficacy.
limitation: Does not cover every cognitive need or native-platform behavior; requires manual assistive-technology testing.
license_data_availability: W3C document licence permits use with attribution; official normative text openly available.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Set WCAG 2.2 AA as release gate; Quran audio needs transcripts/visual state, controls need accessible names, tajwid color must have text/symbol redundancy.

citation: Ok, M. W., Rao, K., Bryant, B. R., & McDougall, D. Universal Design for Learning in Pre-K to Grade 12 Classrooms: A Systematic Review of Research. Exceptionality, 25(2), 116-138.
population_language: Pre-K to grade 12 learners, including students with disabilities; 13 qualifying studies
method: Systematic review of UDL-based classroom interventions and outcomes
finding: UDL interventions sometimes improved access, engagement and academic/social outcomes, but effects ranged from small to large and implementation reporting was inconsistent.
causal_interpretation: Evidence supports UDL as promising, not a proven universal package.
limitation: Only 13 studies; variable designs and weak mapping from claimed UDL to concrete components.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; no open pooled dataset.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Provide multiple representation/action modes, but evaluate each feature; allow audio, text, slowed playback, larger script and alternative non-speech responses without assuming 'UDL' guarantees learning.

citation: Zhang, L., Carter, R. A., Greene, J. A., & Bernacki, M. L. Unraveling Challenges with the Implementation of Universal Design for Learning: A Systematic Literature Review. Educational Psychology Review, 36, 35.
population_language: Educational settings implementing UDL across learner groups
method: Systematic literature review focused on implementation barriers and fidelity
finding: UDL adoption is often constrained by vague operationalization, training demands, time and inconsistent implementation fidelity.
causal_interpretation: Implementation findings do not estimate a single causal learning effect.
limitation: Heterogeneous settings and self-reported implementation; framework labels may mask different interventions.
license_data_availability: Publisher copyright; article access may vary; no reusable implementation dataset stated.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Define concrete accessibility behavior per lesson and audit fidelity; do not use a generic 'accessible mode' toggle as evidence.

citation: Almeqdad, Q. I., Alodat, A. M., Alquraan, M. F., Mohaidat, M. A., & Al-Makhzoomy, A. K. The effectiveness of universal design for learning: A systematic review of the literature and meta-analysis. Cogent Education, 10(1), 2218191.
population_language: Empirical UDL studies published in English or Arabic, 2015-2021
method: Systematic review and meta-analysis across educational settings
finding: The pooled literature suggests positive outcomes, with substantial variability in population, implementation and measures.
causal_interpretation: Average effects cannot identify which UDL component caused improvement.
limitation: Study quality, publication bias and intervention heterogeneity limit precision; little Quran-specific evidence.
license_data_availability: Open access, CC BY 4.0.
concrete_implication_for_muslingo: Run component-level accessibility tests with disabled learners and track task success, not only satisfaction or compliance checklists.
